title: Microsoft
summary: Problems whose patterns are commonly reported in Microsoft coding interviews, from Easy to Hard. Approximate and hand curated, not an official or verified question list.
lesson:
About this list
- Each problem practices a pattern that candidates commonly describe from Microsoft technical interviews: linked-list pointer manipulation, binary tree traversals and serialization, matrix transformations, string parsing, sliding windows, iterators, and cache design.
- Problems are grouped Easy, Medium, and Hard so you can build confidence on core fundamentals before tackling hard pointer, tree, and cache problems.
- The selection is approximate. Interview prompts evolve and vary by team, so treat this track as well-rounded computer-science fundamentals practice rather than a prediction of what you will be asked.

What to expect
- Candidates often report classic data-structure and algorithm prompts with strong emphasis on clean pointer handling, tree recursion/iteration, string/array edge cases, and readable object-oriented design (iterators, caches, codecs).
- Interviewers commonly probe null/empty inputs, integer overflow, duplicate values, and space complexity (for example, in-place matrix rotation or O(1) extra space linked-list manipulation).
- Explaining your test plan and stepping through a small concrete example by hand is frequently valued as much as the final code.

How to prepare
- Practice iterative and recursive tree traversals, linked-list reversal with dummy head nodes, and two-pointer / sliding-window invariants.
- Write clean, modular helper methods rather than cramming state into one loop, and double-check off-by-one bounds on matrix layers and array slices.
- Dry-run edge cases aloud: null/empty inputs, single-node trees or lists, all-negative arrays, and ties.
